children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to open on positive note on November 26, tracking GIFT Nifty, which is trading higher at 26,042 in early trade.
Track the latest updates on GIFT Nifty right here on Moneycontrol

Indian benchmark indices started the December series on a strong note, ending higher on November 25 and recovering from Monday's sharp selloff. The rally was supported by sustained foreign fund inflows, easing crude oil prices and buying interest across select sectors, particularly FMCG and financial stocks.
At close, the Sensex surged 1,502.29 points, or 1.82 percent, to 83,938.28, while the Nifty gained 469.60 points, or 1.85 percent, to settle at 25,819.25.

Among the Nifty 50 constituents, Hindustan Unilever (HUL), Nestle India, Tata Consumer Products, InterGlobe Aviation and HDFC Life Insurance were the biggest gainers. On the other hand, Tata Steel, Shriram Finance, Hindalco Industries, JSW Steel and Max Healthcare were among the top laggards.

Sectorally, FMCG led the rally, surging 2.88 percent, followed by the Private Bank index, which gained 2.2 percent. Pharma advanced 1.7 percent, Auto rose 1 percent and IT added 0.8 percent. In contrast, Media plunged 4.3 percent, while Metal declined 2 percent.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Rises)
GIFT Nifty was trading higher at around 26,042.00 in early trade, indicating a positive start for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Markets (Up)
Asian stocks rose after dip buyers helped drive a late recovery on Wall Street, bringing some stability to markets after doubts over the artificial intelligence trade spurred a flight to Treasuries.

MSCI Inc.’s Asia Pacific equities gauge rose 0.7%, with seven of the gauge’s subsectors advancing. It was only the second advance for the gauge in 11 sessions. That was helped by a 1.8% rally in South Korea’s Kospi and a 1.4% jump in the Nikkei 225 in Japan.
US Equities (Mixed)
The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq retreated on Wednesday amid an AI-related selloff, but finished well off the day's ​lows as bargain hunters stepped in ahead of the US Thanksgiving holiday.
The Dow finished higher.
The Nasdaq fell more than 4% early in ‌the session as the selloff in AI-related stocks and new US tariff proposals hit sentiment.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 164.25 points, or 0.33%, to 50,182.95, the S&P 500 lost 18.31 points, or 0.25%, to ​7,182.78 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 147.73 points, or 0.62%, to 23,585.80.
Dollar Index (Up)

The dollar was steady in Asian trading on Thursday after dropping to a one-week low overnight, as falling Treasury yields and fragile risk sentiment offset the greenback's usual safe-haven appeal ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.
The US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was flat at 103.7.
US Bond Yield (Flat)
The yield on 10-year Treasuries and 2-year Treasury bonds were unchanged at 4.85% and 4.64%, respectively.
Asian currencies (Mixed)

Asian currencies traded on a mixed note against the US dollar, with the Indonesian rupiah emerging as the worst performer, declining 0.56 percent. The Chinese renminbi and Thai baht also weakened by 0.04 percent and 0.02 percent, respectively, while the Singapore dollar slipped 0.02 percent. On the other hand, the Taiwan dollar gained 0.12 percent, followed by the Japanese yen, which rose 0.10 percent. The Malaysian ringgit, Philippine peso and South Korean won also edged higher by 0.07 percent, 0.03 percent and 0.02 percent, respectively.
Crude (Gains)
Oil held a two-day gain as continued hostilities in the Middle East threatened to disrupt the recovery in the region’s crude exports.
Brent traded around $95 a barrel after rising almost 6% over the previous two sessions. West Texas Intermediate was near $84.
Gold (Down)
Gold edged lower, after rising on Wednesday, as inflation data reinforced bets the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates further.
Bullion was near $3,575 an ounce, after briefly slipping below $3,500 an ounce in the previous session before closing up 0.9%.
Fund Flow Action

Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) turned net buyers on November 25, purchasing equities worth Rs 4,018 crore. Meanwhile, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) extended their buying streak for the 11th consecutive session, buying equities worth Rs 4,479 crore.
